People: Dante Alighieri (author, Wikidata Q1067), died 1321; Gustave Doré (illustrator, Wikidata Q6682), died 1883; Henry Francis Cary (translator, Wikidata Q1961974), died 1844. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Dante Alighieri, 1265-1321; Doré, Gustave, 1832-1883 [Illustrator]; Cary, Henry Francis, 1772-1844 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Dante's inferno: translated by Henry Francis Cary from the original of Dante Alighieri, New York: Cassell, [188-?], the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/DantesInfernoTranslatedByHenryFrancisCaryFromTheOriginalOfDante. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 83%, 78%, 82% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Gustave Doré, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
